description: Demography is a crucial branch of geography that studies population size, structure, and distribution. Based on the Census of India 2011, data regarding literacy, sex ratio, and urbanization are highly significant for competitive examinations.

sections.title: Literacy Rate
sections.description: Literacy is a primary indicator of the socio-economic development of any country.

key_concepts.explanation: Any person aged 7 years and above who can read and write with understanding in any language is treated as literate. Children below 7 years of age are treated as illiterate, even if they can read and write.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: State with the highest Literacy Rate in India (94.0%).
State with the lowest Literacy Rate in India (61.8%).
Union Territory with the highest Literacy Rate in India (91.85%).

important_facts.fact: According to the 2011 Census, the total literacy rate of India is 74.04%, with male literacy at 82.14% and female literacy at 65.46%.

sections.title: Sex Ratio
sections.description: It measures the balance between males and females in a society and serves as a vital indicator of the status of women.

key_concepts.explanation: Defined as the number of females per 1000 males in the population.
Defined as the number of females per 1000 males in the age group of 0 to 6 years.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: State with the highest Sex Ratio in India (1084 females per 1000 males).
State with the lowest Sex Ratio in India (879 females per 1000 males).
Union Territory with the highest Sex Ratio in India (1037 females per 1000 males).

important_facts.fact: As per the 2011 Census, the national average Sex Ratio of India is 943, while the Child Sex Ratio (CSR) stands at 919.

sections.title: Urbanization
sections.description: The shift of population from rural to urban areas and the subsequent development of urban centers.

key_concepts.explanation: All places with a municipality, municipal corporation, cantonment board, or notified town area committee.

Places that satisfy three criteria: a minimum population of 5,000; at least 75% of the male main working population engaged in non-agricultural pursuits; and a population density of at least 400 persons per sq. km.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: The most urbanized state in India by percentage (62.17% of its population lives in urban areas).
The state with the highest urban population in terms of absolute numbers.
The least urbanized state in India, having the highest rural population percentage (89.97%).

important_facts.fact: The total urban population in India is 31.16%, while the rural population constitutes 68.84%.
The total number of million-plus cities (Urban Agglomerations with a population of more than 1 million) in India was 53 in 2011.

sections.title: History and Administrative Structure of Census of India
sections.description: The historical background and constitutional provisions regarding demographic data collection in India.

historical_events.significance: India's first non-synchronous census was conducted during the tenure of Lord Mayo.
The first complete and synchronous census was held under Lord Ripon. Since then, the census has been conducted uninterruptedly every 10 years.
During the 1911-1921 decade, India recorded a negative population growth rate (-0.31%). Hence, the year 1921 is known as the demographic divide in Indian demographic history.

polity_articles.provision: Census is a Union List subject.
polity_articles.details: It is mentioned in Entry 69 of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution, giving the Parliament the exclusive right to legislate on matters related to the census.

key_associations.item: Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India
key_associations.extra_info: This organization is responsible for conducting the decennial census and publishing demographic data in India.
